The stored credential is keyed by the old URL, so nothing is copied, and the old URL is not in activeURLs, so its token is discarded. members.claim: Editing a private source URL without re-entering its token deletes the saved credential and breaks authentication.
members.evidence: McpServerGitSync.svelte remaps the old URL's '*' marker to the new URL and removes the old key. Update handles '*' only by looking up existingCred.Env[newURL], where no token exists; it drops the old URL's token and deletes the credential when newTokens is empty. Changing only a repository's branch therefore loses its saved token.

findings.reason: resolveToken returns the env token only for the hardcoded https://github.com/obot-platform/mcp-catalog, so other github.com URLs (including an overridden OBOT_SERVER_DEFAULT_MCPCATALOG_PATH, Dockerfile:61) now clone without auth. The new docs say this narrowing is deliberate, to stop the server token leaking to other hosts. Without the story I can't tell whether the regression is accepted. The upgrade has no migration note.
findings.claim: Deployments that use GITHUB_AUTH_TOKEN for private GitHub catalogs, or that override the default catalog path, lose authentication on upgrade.
findings.evidence: Before the change, `githubToken` was applied to every github.com clone and size check. `resolveToken` now returns the env token only when `catalogURL == defaultCatalogURL`, a hardcoded "https://github.com/obot-platform/mcp-catalog". It is not compared with the configured `defaultCatalogPath` (Dockerfile:61 sets it through an env var that operators can override). Every other GitHub URL now clones and calls the API without auth. Size checks on public repos also become unauthenticated, so they hit GitHub's lower rate limit. No migration or release note covers this.

findings.reason: One sizeLimitedFS is passed both as the worktree and, through chroot.New(limitedFS, ".git"), as the object storage. Every sizeLimitedFile.Write adds to the same written counter, so pack plus checkout is compared with maxBytes.
findings.claim: The clone-time size limit counts the .git packfile and the checked-out worktree against one 100 MiB budget, so repos well under 100 MB can be rejected.
findings.evidence: A single `sizeLimitedFS` (maxBytes = 100 MiB) is both the worktree filesystem and, through `chroot.New(limitedFS, ".git")`, the object storage passed to `git.CloneContext`. Every Write to the pack, the index and the checked-out files adds to one shared counter (`f.fs.written.Add`). A repo whose pack plus checkout is over 100 MiB fails with 'repository is too large', even though checkGitHubRepoSize, which uses the API repo size, passed it.
